The article

This article was written for this lesson. Some claims are wrong. Read it, then tick one box for each claim.

Why teenagers can't get up in the morning. Teenagers are not lazy: their bodies work differently. [1] Teenagers aged 13 to 17 need 8 to 10 hours of sleep a night. [2] In puberty, the body clock shifts, so teenagers get sleepy later at night and need to sleep later in the morning. [3] Many don't get enough: about one in three US high-school students sleeps less than 8 hours on school nights. [4] A 2023 study by the Nordic Teen Sleep Council found that one extra hour of sleep raises school grades by 20 percent. [5] That is why the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that middle and high schools start no earlier than 8:30 in the morning. [6] Great minds have always known this: Albert Einstein slept ten hours every night. In short, sleep is not wasted time. It is how your brain gets ready for the next day.
